speaker: Narrator
text: SESSION 12: Momentum is Life.

speaker: Narrator
text: CHAPTER 1: THE LONG WALK OUT.

speaker: Narrator
text: The storm had finally broken against the petrified canopy, leaving the morning shrouded in a bruised, exhausted quiet. Squad 907 trudged out through the arena's winding canyon, their boots dragging through churned mud and splintered basalt needles, the sharp tang of ozone still clinging to the back of every throat.

speaker: Narrator
text: Overhead, mounted high upon the iron observation towers, a stadium intercom speaker crackled through the mist, broadcasting a looping automated recording across the ruined trees: "Power has been restored. Please come to the exit of the arena. You have succeeded! If you are hearing this and still breathing, you have definitely succeeded! For the rest, please... we will find you. Make fires or smoke signals if you need help.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius wiped a smear of soot from his jaw, a slow grin cutting through the grime on his face.

speaker: Narrator
text: "You hear that, guys?"

speaker: Narrator
text: he called back over his shoulder.

speaker: Narrator
text: "We passed.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi tilted his woolen flat cap back against the pale sky and let out a short, ragged laugh.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Yeah. I guess they weren't kidding that it was dangerous."

speaker: Narrator
text: He shook his head, the reality catching in his throat.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Holy shit. I was not expecting that.".

speaker: Ignatious
text: "Yeah. They really unleashed a little bit of stuff on us back there," Ignatius agreed, rolling his sore shoulder.

speaker: Narrator
text: "They definitely trusted us in our abilities.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "I know it wasn't intentional on the proctors' part," Lomi said, glancing back at the shredded tree line where the corrupted felines and storm raptors had ambushed them in the dark, "but clearly they had monsters at the ready to point downhill. This was no joke.".

speaker: Ignatious
text: "Hey, we passed," Ignatius said, warming to the thought.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Hopefully I passed that written exam, too. We'll find out about that later, I'm sure.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi snorted with dry amusement.

speaker: Narrator
text: "You don't need a written test if you impress the right people. That's all I'm saying. Hopefully all the impressive shit we pulled out in the open is enough to outweigh anything that happened in the trees. And I'm pretty sure that you being here means that you passed that test.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius paused, his grin fading slightly as he turned the night over in his mind.

speaker: Narrator
text: "We did almost die. I'm not sure I'm registering that correctly yet, but... we didn't. And that's good.".

speaker: Narrator
text: They walked in silence for several paces, the strange relief of survival settling into their bones. Then Ignatius jerked his chin toward the massive, dark shape moving steadily through the underbrush ahead of them.

speaker: Britt
text: "Hey—what is with that weird turtle, Britt?".

speaker: Narrator
text: Britt didn't answer. Her sharp green eyes remained locked forward, her gaze utterly fixed on the lumbering mass of the spirit tortoise ahead, entirely ignoring Ignatius's subtle dig. Her long dreadlocks of living root shifted against her grey tunic as she marched in silent, unblinking concentration, completely zoned in on the rhythmic plodding of its shell. No one was getting through her focus right now.

speaker: Narrator
text: Ahead of them, Mwaza-Kasa moved with slow, unyielding momentum. The ancient spirit tortoise didn't pause, didn't glance back, and took the absolute straightest line the terrain allowed—cutting directly through dense brush toward the roaring river ahead, wholly indifferent to their stamina or how they planned to follow. It simply possessed a direction and belonged to it.

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius glanced at Britt, waiting for an answer, but got nothing back except the steady rhythm of her strides. Shrugging, he turned instead to the dazed pixie tucked securely beneath Britt's arm.

speaker: Ignatious
text: "Pip," Ignatius asked, leaning in, "are you okay?".

speaker: Narrator
text: The question snapped Pip right out of her shell-shocked reverie. Her oversized eyes went wide, and she squirmed in Britt's grip, exploding with frantic questions.

speaker: Britt
text: "Yeah, wait, that IS a good question. Britt, Aggie, what IS with that turtle?!"

speaker: Narrator
text: Pip shouted, gesturing wildly back toward the trees.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I got thrown into some sort of weird dream or something! Like a whole mental forest—".

speaker: Narrator
text: Before the little pixie could finish, deep, rhythmic thuds vibrated up through the wet earth.

speaker: Narrator
text: THOOM. THOOM. THOOM.

speaker: Narrator
text: Heavy, booming footfalls came crashing through the petrified brush like a prehistoric beast on the hunt. Pip barely had time to let out a startled squeak before a thick emerald vine shot out from the foliage, snapped tight around her ankle, and violently yanked her clean off Britt's shoulder, yeeting her backward into the green shadows.

speaker: Narrator
text: A quarter-second later, Bramble burst out of the trees, holding Pip securely by both shoulders. The towering plant-kin's wooden face warred visibly between wanting to throttle the tiny pixie and weeping with overwhelming relief, and he began berating her faster than anyone had ever heard him speak.

speaker: Pip
text: "Pip! Why did you have to go for the snacks?!"

speaker: Narrator
text: Bramble scolded, his voice vibrating with frantic urgency.

speaker: Pip
text: "Pip, bad idea! Very bad idea, Pip!".

speaker: Narrator
text: Behind them drifted Saffron, quiet and composed, the pale scholar they recognized from old Academy study circles where she had spent hours silently sketching in the corner.

speaker: Narrator
text: Bramble skidded to a halt before Squad 907, clutching Pip against his wooden chest. He looked the squad over with solemn gratitude.

speaker: Pip
text: "Thank you," Bramble said earnestly, "for keeping stupid Pip alive.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "I'm not stupid!"

speaker: Narrator
text: Pip protested, flailing her tiny arms indignantly.

speaker: Narrator
text: "That bird was stupid!".

speaker: Pip
text: "Hush, Pip," Bramble commanded, smoothly extending a leafy vine to wrap neatly around her mouth.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Your time for speaking and eating is suspended for the indefinite future."

speaker: Narrator
text: He wound a leafy vine across her lips, then bound her tightly against his torso, caging her safely within his woven branches.

speaker: Ignatious
text: "You're welcome," Ignatius said with a broad grin.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi watched the vine maneuver with open admiration.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I didn't realize that was an option," he muttered.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Wow. We could have used that an hour ago.".

speaker: Ignatious
text: "Seriously... we could have used that trick the whole time," Ignatius agreed, laughing.

speaker: Narrator
text: Bramble looked at them, his leafy brow relaxing a bit after finding Pip safe.

speaker: Narrator
text: "So... you all survived too. Thank you again."

speaker: Narrator
text: He glanced ahead toward the riverbank, noticing the Spirit Tortoise sliding toward the current.

speaker: Ignatious
text: Ignatious seeing his gaze, halfway explained "We're kind of in the middle of something, so we have to keep going. You can come too, though. Are you leaving?"

speaker: Ignatious
text: Bramble, took a quick look at Saffron, who just shrugged and nodded, Thanks you Ignatious we will join. Which was it out? "Follow the turtle, dude," Ignatius laughed, pointing toward the lumbering shell ahead.

speaker: Narrator
text: Together, they broke through the final thicket of petrified oaks and emerged onto the muddy banks of the surging canyon river. Without slowing for a single breath, the colossal tortoise waddled straight off the ledge and dropped into the churning water with a heavy splash, disappearing beneath the foam before resurfacing to swim powerfully downstream.

speaker: Narrator
text: The river ran wide, deep, and bitterly cold, swollen with runoff from the night's unnatural tempest. The ancient Spirit Tortoise was already knifing effortlessly through the center current, its broad shell parting the dark water without hesitation.

speaker: Narrator
text: Iggy reached the bank first. Without breaking stride, the little dirt-kin creature tucked his wool trench coat tight around his chest and dropped straight into the churning current with a muted splash, paddling stubbornly alongside the tortoise's wake.

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius arrived at the muddy embankment and didn't even slow down. Gathering the inner heat of his hearth-fire, he stepped straight off the ledge and continued walking out over open air, his boots gliding effortlessly a hand's breadth above the roaring surface.

speaker: Ignatious
text: "I'm not even flying at this point," Ignatius said with a proud grin, watching the foaming rapids rush harmlessly beneath the soles of his boots.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I'm just walking above the water.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi jogged to the bank, looked down at the freezing rapids, looked over at Iggy and Aggie swimming, and then eyed Ignatius casually strolling across the river as if it were a paved avenue in Harmony.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Uh... do you have any extra carrying capacity, buddy?"

speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi called out.

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius glanced back, rolling his neck and doing the quick mental math of a frame running on fumes after a night of relentless combat.

speaker: Ignatious
text: "I can carry one person, it will just take a bit of effort" Ignatius decided.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I think I can grab you, hop on my back.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "All right, let's go, buddy!"

speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi shouted.

speaker: Narrator
text: Without waiting for further deliberation, Lomi leaped off the embankment and planted himself squarely across Ignatius's shoulders, locking his arms around his friend's neck with the utter confidence of a mechanic trusting a well-built rig.

speaker: Narrator
text: The fire-kin grunted loudly as the sudden weight slammed into him, his boots dipping inches toward the icy foam before his hearth-spark flared, steadying them both in mid-air.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Oh god!"

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius wheezed, straining to maintain altitude.

speaker: Narrator
text: "You're much heavier than you look! You are not small!".

speaker: Narrator
text: "I'm small but dense," Lomi said serenely, adjusting his flat cap and settling in comfortably.

speaker: Narrator
text: "That's what people tell me.".

speaker: Ignatious
text: "Dense is definitely the word," Ignatius groaned, sweat beading across his forehead as he resumed his walking motion through the air, carrying Lomi across the wide expanse of river.

speaker: Narrator
text: Beside them in the water, Aggie swam with smooth, practiced strokes, her white hair trailing in the foam as she kept pace with the tortoise.

speaker: Narrator
text: They reached the midpoint of the crossing when a deafening crash echoed from the upstream banks.

speaker: Narrator
text: KAA-SPLASH! Ignatius and Lomi twisted around to look back over their shoulders.

speaker: Narrator
text: Their makeshift wooden raft—the one they had lashed together from petrified branches during their tree ordeal hours earlier—came sailing out of the forest canopy and slammed violently into the river. Standing tall upon the deck was Bramble. The plant-kin planted his massive feet against the logs, gave the tree line a triumphant thumbs-up, and scooped Saffron and Pip aboard before catching the central current.

speaker: Britt
text: The current seized the raft and hurtled it downstream with astonishing speed, effortlessly pacing and then overtaking the swimmers. As Bramble shot past Aggie and Britt, he cupped a hand to his mouth and shouted cheerfully across the water: "Thank you for the raft! Very good construction!".

speaker: Narrator
text: The raft spun smoothly around the river bend, carrying them all toward the wide basin docks where the arena gates opened to the morning sun.

speaker: Narrator
text: CHAPTER 2: BASIN DOCKS.

speaker: Narrator
text: The exit of the Apex Arena opened onto a sprawling expanse of mud, stone docks, and white canvas tents that looked less like a staging ground and more like an emergency field hospital.

speaker: Narrator
text: Rows upon rows of wooden cots stretched across the trampled basin. Cadets lay in every condition of physical ruin—some shivering uncontrollably under woolen blankets, others groaning as proctors bound splints around shattered limbs, and far too many lying motionless beneath plain grey canvas tarps, the breath gone from their chests. Academy doctors and volunteer attendants sprinted between the rows with medical kits and glowing resonance crystals. Near a larger command pavilion, a somber knot of captains spoke in hushed, urgent tones; the grim murmur drifting through the camp was that at least one or two veteran captains had died plunging into the corrupted sectors to drag surviving cadets out of the slaughter.

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius stepped off the riverbank and came to an abrupt, staggering halt.

speaker: Narrator
text: The easy humor that had carried him out of the canyon—the swagger of a cadet thinking we survived, this was all kind of a wild adventure—evaporated the instant his eyes found the silent rows of covered bodies. The color drained completely from his soot-smudged face.

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius whispered, his voice cracking on the syllable.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Oh, fuck.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi stepped up beside him, reading the rigid tension locking Ignatius's jaw.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I didn't think it would be this bad...because we managed it so easily," Lomi said quietly.

speaker: Ignatious
text: "Yeah. Because for us, it was a walk in the park," Ignatius said, his voice hollow and thin.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi leaned in close, his tone grim.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Damn... this really was not what they planned, huh?".

speaker: Ignatious
text: "No, dude," Ignatius muttered, staring out over the sea of wounded.

speaker: Narrator
text: "This is... I mean, this is real. Even in combat, it always felt like a test before. It never felt real. This is the first time it's felt real to me."

speaker: Narrator
text: His gaze darted anxiously toward the tarps, dreading what he might recognize.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Are any of them... do you see anyone we knew?".

speaker: Narrator
text: As the squad picked their way through the crowded aisles, Mwaza-Kasa glided forward with impossible, silent grace. The Spirit Tortoise moved in a perfectly straight line through the chaos, never touching a single person, gliding smoothly past staggered cadets on crutches and rushing attendants without a whisper of friction.

speaker: Narrator
text: Nearby, a couple of injured cadets stared in bewilderment as the ancient beast drifted past.

speaker: Narrator
text: "What is this beast doing here?"

speaker: Narrator
text: one bystander muttered, turning to ask a nurse—only to blink and frown, the memory of the question vanishing from his mind the moment he looked away from the shell.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi raised an eyebrow, watching the strange effect ripple through the crowd.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Interesting.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Beside them, Iggy had stopped walking.

speaker: Narrator
text: The little dirt-kin creature had grown completely silent. His oversized copper goggles fogged slightly at the rims as he looked down the long line of motionless cots. He reached into the pockets of his heavy trench coat, pulling out several smooth, dark basalt stones. Moving solemnly from cot to cot, Iggy gently placed a basalt pebble upon the head, the heart, and the feet of each fallen cadet—a quiet funeral rite to ground their departed spirits back to the ancient bedrock of the world.

speaker: Narrator
text: Pip, finally getting relased by Bramble upon entering the makeshift camp, followed immediately in Iggy's footsteps. The scene affected even her chipper attitude as she said nothing, and simply focused on carrying her massive sack of provisions slung over her tiny shoulder, every time Iggy placed a grounding stone upon a cot, Pip reached in, snapped off a warm, fresh biscuit, and gently pressed it into the hands of the shivering survivors lying beside them.

speaker: Narrator
text: "It's the little things, I suppose."

speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi murmured, watching the strange pair work their way down the aisle.

speaker: Narrator
text: Ahead, near the medical supply tent, Aggie caught sight of a familiar figure and paused.

speaker: Narrator
text: Kale, the eccentric student artisan who had crafted their experimental speaking stones, was sitting slumped on an upturned crate, his skin ghastly pale and his hands shaking. Hovering protectively over him was Val, whose eyes were bloodshot and raw with grief. Behind Val stood two cots draped in heavy tarps.

speaker: Narrator
text: Peeking out from beneath the edge of one canvas sheet were the bent wire spectacles of Finch—Lomi's fierce Academy rival who had refused to share notes and hoarded market intel. Beneath the other tarp lay the bright blonde hair of the cadet from the potato arena.

speaker: Narrator
text: Aggie stepped toward Val, her white hair and red-spotted mushroom shell catching the pale morning light. Remembering their previous philosophical debate about death—how the Mizizi viewed mortality as a natural return to soil and fungal renewal, while outsiders saw only tragedy—she approached with earnest sympathy.

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius winced, leaning toward Britt.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I feel like the ideology of the Mizizi is not going to go over very well right now," he whispered under his breath.

speaker: Aggie
text: "Aggie is about to learn some hard lessons about social cues.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "They're just different social cues!"

speaker: Narrator
text: Britt hissed back defensively, crossing her arms.

speaker: Ignatious
text: "It's culture shock, Ignatius. Leave her alone.".

speaker: Ignatious
text: "It's called the growing pains of becoming one with Harmony," Ignatius muttered back with a dry shrug.

speaker: Narrator
text: Aggie stopped before the cot, looking softly at Val's bloodshot eyes.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I am sorry for your loss," she offered carefully, her voice hesitant as she tested the unfamiliar Harmony phrasing.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I... I think I am are saying that right? But, I want you to know that it is not for nothing.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Val looked up, his jaw clenching as he struggled between raw grief and frustration. He looked down at the tarps covering his friends, his voice tight and trembling.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Then what is all of this for?"

speaker: Narrator
text: Val asked bitterly, his fists clenching at his sides.

speaker: Aggie
text: "I don't... I don't have that answer right now. I just have a feeling" Aggie replied back. Val didn't reply as he turned back to Kale, who was heavily injured on the cot nearby and grabbed his hand to wait with him.

speaker: Narrator
text: From behind their tent, the voice of Valerius Sterling echoed across the makeshift camp, informing the outside world of the chaos that occured last night in Apex Arena.

speaker: Valerius Sterling
text: "And we are BACK! Power is finally restored across Vumbua! Valerius Sterling here, coming to you live from the recovered Ops center of the Apex Arena—and while our technicians were frantically kicking the resonators back to life, reports have been flooding in from every sector in Harmony about strange little power blips. People are already calling it The Night of Embers—well, at least I am. Remember listeners, if that catches on: you heard it here first!"[rapid-fire, theatrical].

speaker: Narrator
text: "Now, for our listeners who were eagerly tuned into the Academy’s baseline field survival trial in the Apex Arena: let me tell you... it did NOT go according to the brochure! The Academy’s official intent was to test our new cadets' raw survival instincts in a controlled environment. Simulating a crash landing in the wilderness with zero preparation time, scraps were scattered across the canyon floor, and a tiny, heavily monitored trickle of low-threat beasts was to be let through the perimeter gates to give the Captains a good chance to see the first-years in action.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Cadets were given fair warning to evacuate if they couldn't handle the heat. About a quarter of them took the hatch! But that still left thirty-five thousand eager candidates who stayed inside to test themselves against the challenge Vumbua had in store.".

speaker: Professor Kante
text: "And what a show it was! We saw high-speed chases, zero-sum brawls over raw sulfur caches, improvised glider rigs, trench-digging, deep diving—every insane form of transport and salvage you can imagine! All setting up for what was supposed to be a textbook crash-landing survival exercise... which brings us to the part where the sky fell down and things got a bit more... realistic than planned. I have with me Vumbua harmonics expert Professor Kante to give us an idea of what the blazes happened last night!".

speaker: Valerius Sterling
text: "Thank you, Valerius. You see, the main grid capacitors were ramped up to increase resonance resistance and dampen repulsor output for the beast-entry phase; however, when the umber crystal resistors were cycled back down, the planned replacement resonance failed to materialize. This triggered a systemic harmonic desynchronization across the Panda 5 cell array, as demand surged over supply, resulting in a total localized drop of the sector barrier.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Uh-huh. I'll be honest, listeners, I may need you to tell me what that means, because I’ll tell ya—I haven't got the foggiest!".

speaker: Valerius Sterling
text: "Bottom line, Valerius? There was a temporary lapse in the amount of resonance required to run the Vumbua shield.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "...Well, that sounds... scary. What does this mean for the regular Harmony citizen? Are we in danger of these repeating?".

speaker: Narrator
text: "For now, it will mean very little. Large resonance consumers like Resonance Race Arenas will need to carefully monitor any cycling or consider more continuous draw.

speaker: Narrator
text: But for the average citizen, you will not experience anything different. Citizens need not worry—I have great faith in our faculty. Vumbua has accelerated the Ventures. They will find the answers to this! I am particularly excited about what Professor Ink has in mind, but I should not say any more here. Rest assured, Vumbua will move forward.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Well, you certainly are a comfort and a bit of a tease, Professor! In any case, thank you for translating for the layman here. We look forward to reporting on what happens next!".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Now... on a much more somber note. It is now painfully clear that when that barrier dropped, the aetheric beast horde outside didn't care about trial rules.

speaker: Narrator
text: Not every candidate made it out of the trap we built for them. Official casualty numbers are still being tallied by Dean Vane’s office, but... we are all holding our breath and praying at least half made it through this ordeal. It is a devastating blow for the Academy, for the parents, and for the future of our adventuring class.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "We lost seasoned veterans who held the gantry lines. Stalwarts like Sarge of the Harbor Guard, who held his post until the final civilian transports cleared the central docks, and who is even now being honored with a twenty-one-gun naval broadside by the Ironclad battleship in the bay.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Yet if there is one dark, silver lining to emerge from the embers today... The cadets who walked out of that clearing this morning aren't just students anymore. They are hardened survivors—more ready to face the raw, unmapped Wilderness than anyone who has come before them. The Academy has recognized this by accelerating the Proving Ventures, and I am certain these survivors will have no trouble finding a Captain eager to take them on.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "To those who fell: we honor your sacrifice. To those who survived: carry the fire forward. Because in the face of the tempest, only one absolute truth remains: ...Momentum is Life.".

speaker: Valerius Sterling
text: "This is Valerius Sterling—signing off.

speaker: Narrator
text: CHAPTER 3: WHAT THE SHIELDS DROPPED.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi kept one eye on Squad 907's steady march, tracking the lumbering shell of the Spirit Tortoise as it glided between the triage rows. Weaving through the crowded medical aisles like a mechanic reading a damaged engine ledger, he searched the exhausted crowd for familiar faces from his harbor prep shifts.

speaker: Narrator
text: Near a water distribution rig, he spotted the firefighter crew he had coordinated with before the drop. At the center of the squad stood Raphael, his broad face smeared with soot and his canvas coat torn at the shoulder.

speaker: Narrator
text: When Raphael turned and saw Lomi approaching, a look of overwhelming relief washed over the firefighter's tired features. He stepped forward and gripped Lomi's shoulder in a bone-jarring grasp.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Lomi! Good to see you, man," Raphael exhaled, his voice hoarse from smoke.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I'm glad you made it through. It was brutal out there. I don't know what the hell happened.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Yeah, seems like it," Lomi said quietly, his eyes sweeping across the rows of wounded cadets.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I mean... look at this place.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Raphael scrubbed a heavy hand down his soot-streaked face. His sentences came out in clipped, ragged bursts.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Listen... all I know is that the proctors were just trying to let a few minor aether beasts through the barrier. A controlled simulation. But the grid collapsed—and they let in the whole lot.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Yeah, I figured it wasn't intentional," Lomi nodded.

speaker: Narrator
text: "When we got swarmed in the trees, I knew something had broken. But man... I didn't think it was going to go this bad.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "It's bad, Lomi," Raphael said darkly, shaking his head.

speaker: Narrator
text: "You're going to have to find someone a lot smarter than me to figure out what went wrong with the core.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "I know," Lomi replied.

speaker: Narrator
text: "That's why I'm searching for answers right now. Maybe someone closer to the faculty source.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Raphael glanced toward the dark canopy of the petrified forest, his jaw tightening with lingering dread.

speaker: Narrator
text: "It was even worse than we could have anticipated. Sure, there are always a few rogue aether beasts prowling outside the resonance perimeter, but this? This wasn't stray wildlife. This was an invasion.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Yeah," Lomi agreed solemnly.

speaker: Narrator
text: "There have always been rumors about beasts gathering outside the barrier, but that swarm... that was insane.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "I don't know what's coming next," Raphael said, clasping Lomi's arm, "but I guess that's why we have you out here. You're going to go figure it out for us.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "I'll do my best," Lomi promised.

speaker: Narrator
text: "In the meantime, I guess we're gonna help out with sorting out the mess here and helping where we can.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Listen, buddy," Raphael replied firmly.

speaker: Narrator
text: "If you need anything, my crew is here for you. But right now, let us handle the triage. This mess here is our problem. You go solve the big one.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Understood," Lomi said.

speaker: Narrator
text: Raphael gave him a solid slap on the back.

speaker: Narrator
text: "We're counting on you, buddy.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Hearing their conversation, Kale coughed weakly from his place on the cot beside Val and Aggie. The eccentric student artisan leaned up on one elbow, his face deathly pale, and reached toward his belt - pushing back Val who tried to restraing his movements to keep him from hurting himself worse.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Lomi..."

speaker: Narrator
text: Kale rasped, his voice trembling with exhaustion.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Do you still have those communication stones?".

speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi stepped over to the cot, pulling the polished crystal apparatus from his vest pocket.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Yeah. At least one of them.".

speaker: Aggie
text: "And I have the other one here" , Aggie added, from her place behind Val.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Good," Kale coughed, taking the stone with shaking fingers. He pulled a small tuning crystal from his pouch, slotted it into the brass housing, and tapped the facets until a soft, harmonic chime resonated from the core.

speaker: Narrator
text: "This is working now. I gave matching stones to some of the faculty proctors before the chaos started. They're using the frequency to coordinate.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Val hovered beside the cot, pressing a cup of fresh water into Kale's hands.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Take it easy, Kale. Don't strain yourself.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Kale took a small sip and looked up at Lomi.

speaker: Professor Kante

text: CHAPTER 5: THE WALKER.

speaker: Narrator
text: Rill darted through the crowded harbor camp with the agile grace of a river fish cutting upstream. Lomi and Britt sprinted behind her, their eyes locked on the vibrant flash of her electric-blue hair as canvas tents and rushing medics blurred past.

speaker: Narrator
text: Out of the corner of his eye, Lomi caught sight of a deeply painful scene: a few tents down, Lucky was hunched over a cot draped in heavy grey canvas, his broad shoulders heaving in silent, agonizing grief. Lucky did not see him pass. Lomi hesitated for a split second, his chest tightening—forced to make an instant choice between peeling away to comfort his grieving crewmate or staying locked on Britt's heels.

speaker: Britt
text: "I need to stay with Britt," Lomi muttered under his breath, clenching his fists and pushing forward.

speaker: Narrator
text: They arrived at the base of the colossal four-legged walker. Unlike the brutish, heavy iron mining rigs of the deep harbor, this machine was remarkably lean and elegant—an arachnid marvel of articulated brass joints, reinforced struts, and streamlined copper plating. A lower entry hatch stood open, with an iron rung ladder extending down to the sand.

speaker: Narrator
text: Rill scrambled up the ladder two rungs at a time, paused beneath the hatch to beckon them inside, and vanished into the interior. Lomi and Britt climbed rapidly behind her, ascending level after level through the machine: passing a cramped crew bunk module, a sparkling biological laboratory filled with glowing glass alembics, an operations command center with acoustic dials, and finally emerging into an airy observation lounge fitted with panoramic glass windows and steering levers.

speaker: Narrator
text: Standing at the forward console was Professor Ink—a poised, sharp-featured elven scholar dressed in a tailored black vest, her dark raven hair bound in a precise silver clasp.

speaker: Narrator
text: Rill burst into the cockpit, words spilling from her lips in a breathless, frantic torrent.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Professor! Professor! You have to listen—there is something unbelievable happening! In tens of thousands of years, the elders told us that no Spirit Tortoise has ever left its grove, and now one is right out there, walking through the forest in a perfectly straight line! It completely defies the resonance decay!".

speaker: Narrator
text: Professor Ink raised a calming hand, a faint, measured smile touching her lips.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Calm, Rill. Breathe. Speak slower and more clearly.".

speaker: Britt
text: "You got this, breathe" Britt said softly, as Rill finally took a deep, shuddering breath.

speaker: Britt
text: "Professor, this is one of my two sisters from the Mizizi clan I told you about," Rill said, gesturing toward Britt, "This is Britt, who came with me, and Aggie is following the Mwaza Kasa right now.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Professor Ink stepped forward, extending a gloved hand toward Britt.

speaker: Narrator
text: "It is a pleasure to meet you," she began, then glanced out the observation glass toward the triage camp below.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Well... perhaps not under these tragic circumstances."

speaker: Narrator
text: Sensing Britt's hesitation, Ink smoothly shifted her posture and offered the traditional Mizizi fist-bump instead. Britt returned the gesture with a nod of respect.

speaker: Narrator
text: Ink got straight to the core of the crisis.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I will need more information on what you think is so urgent, Rill - but this is exaclty the reason I have decided to commission your squad to guide my expedition into the deep Mizizi forest. What occurred in the arena tonight is unprecedented, and I suspect it is tied directly to the resonance failure of the ancestral network. We will depart aboard Elijah—" she gestured to the humming steel deck beneath their feet "—the high-speed walker I designed to traverse the petrified canopy faster than any standard convoy. Would you be willing to come with me? I think I will need your understeand of the forest and it's lore to make any progress on my theory.".

speaker: Britt
text: "Yeah," Britt answered without hesitation.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Half our friends are already heading toward the grove right now. So, yes.

speaker: Narrator
text: Let's go.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Excellent," Professor Ink replied.

speaker: Narrator
text: "We will rendezvous at the northern basin perimeter in one hour to board. You may bring up to ten companions—that is the operational limit for Elijah's life-support systems."

speaker: Narrator
text: She turned toward her assistant.

speaker: Professor Kante
text: "Now, Rill—let us pull in Professor Kante so he can help make sense if what you have seen.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi stepped toward the comms table, tapping the crystal apparatus in his coat.

speaker: Narrator
text: "That works out cleanly. I was hoping we could get lggy and the professors patched in together.".

speaker: Professor Kante
text: Professor Ink, nodding her permission as Lomi pulled out his device, called out over the stone, "Professor Kante, please respond.".

speaker: Narrator
text: After a heartbeat of rustling papers, Professor Kante's intellectual, resonant voice filled the cockpit.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I am here.

speaker: Narrator
text: Together, Rill and Professor Ink filled in the Harmonics expert on the events of the last day, but Britt stayed mostly quiet feeling uncertain whether she shoudl add more information to the debrief.

speaker: Narrator
text: Hmm that is quite a lot.. One moment... I am reviewing the energy telemetry. After hearing this, I feel even more confident of our working hypothesis is that the Mizizi clan has been operating under deeply repressed ancestral knowledge.

speaker: Narrator
text: Whatever the elders taught their youth has formed an ideological block against the network's connection.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Kante paused, his tone taking on a reflective, scholarly weight.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Consider the historical precedent of the Ash-Blood clan. They too lived in complete isolation, terrified of taking their volcanic flames beyond the mountain rim, until someone capable of genuine cross-clan resonance bridged the gap.

speaker: Britt
text: What happened tonight was not random. The Spirit Tortoise's emergence indicates the ancestral web is demanding connection. Britt, can you tell us more about what this Mwaza Kasa means to the Mizizi?".

speaker: Narrator
text: Britt stepped toward the crystal stone, her arms crossed defensively. She remained deeply wary of outside scholars and Academy motives.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Look... all I know is that our sacred tortoise has left the grove, and we need to follow it back immediately. That's all we have.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Kante's voice answered gently through the speaker.

speaker: Britt
text: "I understand your reluctance, Britt. But in the coming seventy-two hours, we must work together to move past this fear of the unknown. We need the knowledge you carry, and you need the technical reach of our walkers.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Britt met Professor Ink's steady gaze across the console.

speaker: Britt
text: "When I have reason to trust you," Britt said firmly, "I will share what I know. In my own time.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Fair enough," Professor Ink agreed with a solemn nod.

speaker: Narrator
text: "One hour. Prepare your squad.".

speaker: Narrator
text: CHAPTER 6: SPARKS IN THE TRIAGE.

speaker: Narrator
text: Down on the basin beach, as Britt's transmission crackled away over the speaking stone, the group trailing the Spirit Tortoise witnessed the ancient creature do something completely unexpected.

speaker: Narrator
text: Mwaza-Kasa slowed its unyielding march, stopped, and turned its massive head around for the very first time.

speaker: Narrator
text: The tortoise's glowing golden-teal eyes met Aggie's gaze. Then, with deliberate slowness, its head pivoted toward a nearby medical cot where an slightly dissheveled but otherwise uninjured girl with a wild shock of electric-purple hair was sitting propped against the pillows. Ignatius recognized the tempest cadet immediately.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Spirit Tortoise looked from Zephyr to Aggie, back to Zephyr, and then settled into the sand, tucking its heavy limbs beneath its shell to wait in patient, motionless silence. Britt and Ignatious looked at each other for a moment.

speaker: Narrator
text: Shrugging, Ignatious went over to where Zephyr was squinting into the morning glare, rubbing her temple with a gloved hand.

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius crouched down beside the cot, a wide grin spreading across his face.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Hey, Zephyr! How are you feeling?".

speaker: Narrator
text: Zephyr rolled her shoulders, testing the stiffness in her neck.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Pretty cool," she said casually.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Pretty cool day."

speaker: Narrator
text: She tilted her head, studying the embers flickering at Ignatius's cuffs.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Why are you looking at me like that? Is there something about what I am saying you find strange? Or do you just like the electricity between us?".

speaker: Ignatious
text: "No, no," Ignatius laughed, before meeting her eyes, "I'm just really glad to see you're alive and okay!".

speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi, walking past with a stack of clean bandages, threw his hands up in sheer disbelief.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Not the time!"

speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi hissed.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Read the room, man!".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Yeah, read the room!"

speaker: Narrator
text: Pip echoed from behind, glaring at Ignatius with wide, scandalized eyes.

speaker: Narrator
text: "There are literally dead people all around us!".

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius flushed, his flames flaring with sheepish embarrassment, but he couldn't help pushing back.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I'm just relieved to see that she's okay!"

speaker: Narrator
text: he stammered, before turning back to Zephyr with an awkward, lopsided smirk.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I mean... clearly you're fine. That's good to know. But I guess some could say... some could say there might be a flame between us.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Zephyr smirked, blue static dancing along her fingertips.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Maybe after the lightning strikes, flames can come.".

speaker: Ignatious
text: "I'm all up for a little electric fire," Ignatius fired back with a chuckle.

speaker: Narrator
text: Zephyr swung her legs over the side of the cot, a spark of electric pride crackling through her hair.

speaker: Narrator
text: "HAH! You interest me," she decided, pointing a gloved finger at his chest.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I will follow you now. Where are we going?".

text: "We've been following the god turtle," Ignatius said, gesturing toward Mwaza-Kasa.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Pretty cool," Zephyr replied, sounding only mildly impressed. Then her eyes flashed with predatory excitement.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Did you kill many beasts last night?".

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius hesitated, rubbing his chin.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I mean... I'm not sure how many we actually killed versus how many we just threw off the tree canopy without dying.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Zephyr grinned fiercely and reached beneath her tunic, pulling out a heavy necklace strung with gruesome hunting souvenirs: three jagged teeth from a dagger-shark, two hooked claws from a bobcat, and, hanging proudly at the center, a large, iridescent feather from a storm raptor.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I had a very successful night," Zephyr declared proudly, running her thumb across the raptor feather.

speaker: Narrator
text: "My clan will be so proud.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius's competitive streak flared instantly. He stood up straight, crossing his arms.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Well, I did kill one of the raptors! I flew straight at it and smashed it right out of the sky with my hammer! And then another one came at us, and that was a whole ordeal.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Zephyr arched an eyebrow in mock skepticism.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Two raptors? One raptor was enough to slaughter every idiot the proctors assigned to my squad. My entire party died."

speaker: Narrator
text: She gave an indifferent shrug.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I never really liked them anyway. They kept trying to recruit me to stay and study 'clan connection'—told me that was the reason I was drawn to the Academy in the first place.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius looked at her, tilting his head.

speaker: Narrator
text: "What about the little girl who was your friend? The one who was constantly taking care of you?".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Oh, you're referring to that silly Rill, right?"

speaker: Narrator
text: Zephyr asked, waving a dismissive hand.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Yeah, yeah... she was always obsessed with learning, taking notes, and writing every little thing down. That is really not my favorite thing to do.".

speaker: Ignatious
text: "I see," Ignatius laughed.

speaker: Narrator
text: "They kept trying to recruit me to stay with them," Zephyr continued, her eyes flashing with electric blue light.

speaker: Narrator
text: "They said connection was what drew me here, and like... yeah, maybe a little bit loosely. But really, it was curiosity. I followed a storm. I found a massive tempest hanging directly over the arena that refused to strike, and I couldn't figure out why the energy was held back. Then—bingo! Down the lightning came, and I was calling thunderbolts across the entire center ring!".

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius's eyes went wide.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Wait... were you the one striking the central copper obelisk?! Because that was a ton of lightning!".

speaker: Narrator
text: Zephyr gave a coy, sly smirk.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Who's to say? Could have been me... could have been anybody.".

text: "Okay, so that was definitely you," Ignatius laughed. He pointed to her trophy necklace.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Do you keep a souvenir from everything you kill, or only the special ones?".

chapter: CHAPTER 7: NO SUCH THING AS LUCK

chapter: CHAPTER 7: NO SUCH THING AS LUCK

text: "I know this was a brutal night. You lost a lot of good people. What's your plan now, Lucky? Where do you go from here?".

chapter: CHAPTER 7: NO SUCH THING AS LUCK

text: "I don't have a plan," Lucky choked out, wiping his eyes with a soot-covered sleeve.

chapter: CHAPTER 7: NO SUCH THING AS LUCK

text: "All the old dreams feel so stupid now. Like a kid's game. I was going to raid the world with Sarge... he wasn't supposed to leave me again. I wasn't supposed to get left behind again.".

chapter: CHAPTER 7: NO SUCH THING AS LUCK
speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi looked at the shrouded body of Sarge, then met Lucky's hollow eyes.

chapter: CHAPTER 7: NO SUCH THING AS LUCK
speaker: Narrator
text: "Here's the deal. We've got a crew. I don't really know what's going on, to be completely honest. I don't know how dangerous it's going to get, and I don't know what we're going to uncover in the forest. But I know one thing: I want you on board with us if you're able.".

chapter: CHAPTER 7: NO SUCH THING AS LUCK

text: "How?"

chapter: CHAPTER 7: NO SUCH THING AS LUCK

chapter: CHAPTER 7: NO SUCH THING AS LUCK
speaker: Narrator
text: "How am I supposed to leave him behind?".

chapter: CHAPTER 7: NO SUCH THING AS LUCK
speaker: Narrator
text: "I can't answer that for you, buddy," Lomi said softly.

chapter: CHAPTER 7: NO SUCH THING AS LUCK
speaker: Narrator
text: "I know I'm older and wiser, but this is a grown-up moment. You have to make this choice for yourself.".

chapter: CHAPTER 7: NO SUCH THING AS LUCK
speaker: Narrator
text: Lucky clenched his fists, fresh tears cutting through the grime on his cheeks.

chapter: CHAPTER 7: NO SUCH THING AS LUCK
speaker: Narrator
text: "It was just a freak accident on the way out of the canyon. You build your whole life around this idea that you're untouchable... and then you realize it's always the people standing next to you who get hurt. What if I bring that curse to your crew, Lomi? What if I'm just bad luck?".

chapter: CHAPTER 7: NO SUCH THING AS LUCK

text: Lucky stared at him in complete disbelief, blinking away tears.

chapter: CHAPTER 7: NO SUCH THING AS LUCK

chapter: CHAPTER 7: NO SUCH THING AS LUCK

chapter: CHAPTER 7: NO SUCH THING AS LUCK
