speaker: Narrator
text: CHAPTER 8: THE IRONCLAD SALUTE.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi followed Lucky toward the command pavilion, where a circle of veteran officers stood near the harbor docks. At the center stood an imposing Goliath captain, completely bald, his face etched with ceremonial bridge-tattoos, wearing heavy iron plating riveted into a thick leather duster. Inscribed in polished brass across his chest armor was a single word: IRONCLAD.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lucky approached the captain, his hand outstretched.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Captain... it's about Sarge.".

speaker: Narrator
text: The Goliath nodded with solemn gravity, placing a massive hand over Lucky's shoulder. He flagged down four of his strongest crewmen, who stepped forward with crisp military precision, lifted Sarge's shrouded stretcher onto their broad shoulders, and began an honor jog toward the colossal ironclad battleship moored at the central pier.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi caught a passing dockworker by the sleeve.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Hey, what time is it? It's like five in the morning, right?".

speaker: Narrator
text: The worker glanced at the high morning glare.

speaker: Narrator
text: "It's almost noon, mate. The night storm ate three hours of daylight.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Oh right...got it," Lomi nodded, picking up his pace.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Whatever, I've got time to see this through."

speaker: Narrator
text: Smiling, Lomi jied the procession toward the Ironclad to see Sarge off.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi wasn't the only one to make use of the hour before the crew was set to depart. Across the thinning triage rows, Aggie doubled back to find Val sitting beside Kale's cot. The heavy canvas tarps had been cleared away, leaving Val staring silently into the distance.

speaker: Aggie
text: Val looked up as Aggie approached. Aggie - seeing the hurt in Val's eyes forged ahead with the short speech she had been rehearsing in her head, "Look... I'm sorry. I don't know what to say in a moment like this. And I don't know the why of what happened here. But I think we're going to find out why. We have a connection with our Spirit Tortoise, and it's leading us somewhere.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Val took a moment before responding, his voice quiet and heavy.

speaker: Narrator
text: "There's been a theory spreading through the camp that my father broke the resonance grid when he first discovered your clan's valley," Val murmured, his fists resting on his knees.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I don't know the truth behind any of it. But if your spirit tortoise is moving...

speaker: Narrator
text: is there a chance to set that right?".

speaker: Aggie
text: "I hope so," Aggie said gently.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Whether or not your father was the cause, we need to find the truth.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Val looked at Kale, who gave him a firm, supportive nod. Val stood up, extending a hand to clasp Aggie's.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Then I want to come with you. Lead the way.".

speaker: Narrator
text: The two quickly caught back up with Ignatious who was standing guard at the renedezvous point - mostly making sure Pip didn't run off for snacks before the walker could arrive.

speaker: Narrator
text: Suddenly, a deafening thunderclap ripped across the entire basin.

speaker: Narrator
text: BOOM! BOOM! BOOM! Back across the camp, With his front row seat from the deck of the Ironclad, Lomi watched as a full naval broadside erupted from the massive turrets of the Ironclad battleship. The colossal artillery shells detonated in mid-air over the turquoise water, unleashing a dense, rolling thundercloud of black gunpowder smoke across the bay. A second synchronized barrage fired immediately after, igniting the smoke cloud from within with brilliant resonance pyrotechnics that painted the morning sky in vibrant streaks of crimson, gold, and turquoise.

speaker: Narrator
text: A third salvo cracked like lightning, instantly dispelling the storm cloud in a breathtaking twenty-one-gun salute as Sarge's body was committed to the deep canyon waters.

speaker: Narrator
text: Soon after, Lucky stepped away from the battleship's gangway and jogged up beside Lomi on the beach, his jaw set with fierce resolve.

speaker: Narrator
text: "All right," Lucky said, rolling his shoulders.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I don't know what we're walking into, but I'm ready. Let's do this. Let's go.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Let's do it," Lomi smiled.

speaker: Narrator
text: They sprinted across the sand to where Elijah, Professor Ink's four-legged spider-walker, now stood idling at the forest perimeter.

speaker: Narrator
text: The entire expedition gathered at the base ladder: Britt, Iggy, Ignatius, Lomi, Aggie, Val, Pip, Bramble, Saffron, Zephyr, and Lucky—six extra companions in total. One by one, they scrambled up the iron rungs into the hull.

speaker: Narrator
text: As the lower entry hatch sealed shut with a pressurized hiss, the massive Spirit Tortoise looked up, met Aggie's eyes through the observation glass with a solemn nod, and surged forward—spinning a trail of flattened brush behind it as Elijah's mechanical legs kicked into a galloping sprint, racing straight across the plains towards the ancient Mizizi forest.

speaker: Narrator
text: CHAPTER 9: THE LAB BELOW.

speaker: Narrator
text: Inside the humming hull of the four-legged walker Elijah, the machine settled into a rhythmic, lurching gallop across the savanna grasslands.

speaker: Narrator
text: The main operations compartment opened into a spacious central lounge arranged around a long tactical table. Projecting from the center was an acoustic holographic display showing the vast terrain stretching between Vumbua and the distant Mizizi forest, with a plotted route cutting across the flat plains.

speaker: Narrator
text: While the squad traded quick pleasantries and claimed bunks, Rill stepped over to where Zephyr was lounging near Ignatius, nodding stiffly at the tempest cadet.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I'm glad you're alive," Rill muttered—a courtesy delivered with visible reservation.

speaker: Narrator
text: Then Rill's gaze shifted to Britt, and the color instantly drained from her face. She gasped, slapping a hand against her forehead.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Oh gods... I completely forgot!"

speaker: Narrator
text: Rill exclaimed in sudden panic. She grabbed Britt's forearm with urgent force.

speaker: Britt
text: "Britt, I need you down in the lower laboratory right now! This very second—fast as you can move!".

speaker: Narrator
text: Without waiting for an answer, Rill sprinted across the deck, threw open the floor hatch, and slid down the ladder rungs like a drop of water down a conduit pipe.

speaker: Narrator
text: Britt hurried after her without hesitation, with Aggie dropping through the hatch right behind them. Iggy hovered by the ladder, eyeing Zephyr suspiciously; but seeing the purple-haired cadet cross her boots and lean back for a nap, he decided she wasn't going anywhere. Iggy made a quick, theatrical warding gesture with his soil-stained fingers—a cheeky half-hex to keep her asleep—and scrambled down the ladder after the squad. Ignatius trailed down last, feeling distinctly awkward in the confined research bay.

speaker: Narrator
text: Down in the lower laboratory, Rill rushed to a heavy, reinforced containment safe mounted in the corner. She spun the combination dials, threw back the steel latch, and retrieved a small glass vial filled with a luminous, swirling neon liquid.

speaker: Narrator
text: The glowing fluid inside was the exact iridescent hue as the mysterious substance Britt had discovered in the buried cache where they had recovered the compass.

speaker: Narrator
text: Rill turned around, holding the vial up to the light.

speaker: Britt
text: "Britt... does this liquid look familiar to you?".

speaker: Narrator
text: Britt stared at the shimmering contents, her pulse spiking.

speaker: Britt
text: "Yeah," Britt said grimly.

speaker: Narrator
text: "That looks identical to the substance that caused the fungal rash spreading on my shoulder.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Not good," Rill muttered, her voice trembling as she gestured frantically toward an examination stool.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Not good at all! Sit down, please—sit down right now!".

speaker: Narrator
text: Rill reached into her medical kit and pulled out a second glass vial, this one filled with a dense, shimmering neon-purple tonic. She shoved it into Britt's hands.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Drink this immediately," Rill commanded urgently.

speaker: Narrator
text: "What is this?"

speaker: Narrator
text: Britt asked, looking down at the purple draught.

speaker: Narrator
text: Rill took a deep, shaky breath, leaning against the lab counter.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I was in Professor Ink's laboratory when the field sample was brought in from the ruins. It completely gutted me to recognize it... because this substance comes from the canyon territory where I was raised. Back before the clan exchange that I still can't talk about.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Rill pointed at the glowing vial, her eyes wide with terror.

speaker: Britt
text: "You were exposed to a lethal biological agent that grows in only one isolated canyon gorge. It has a permanent cure, but I can't rememebr exactly how to make it and I wouldn't have what I'd need here anyway. But if you drink this stabilizing tonic once every seven days, it halts the cellular degradation. Because if you don't drink this, Britt... you are going to die in about two weeks.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Britt stared down at the vial, the weight of the diagnosis pressing heavily into her chest. The memory of the ancient vision that the Mwaza Kassa had shown her in the branches of the Arena echoed in her mind—she had seen others suffering from this same wasting illness in the memories of the old world, people who had asked dangerous questions and left the forest canopy.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Has this substance ever come into contact with the Mizizi clan before?"

speaker: Narrator
text: Britt asked carefully.

speaker: Narrator
text: "That should be impossible," Rill answered, shaking her head vigorously.

speaker: Narrator
text: "It grows in only one forbidden canyon cave, and no one ever goes there!".

speaker: Britt
text: "I think I carry memories of our people struggling with this exact condition," Britt pressed, her green eyes boring into Rill's.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Not necessarily the liquid itself, but the illness it causes.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Rill stared at her, baffled.

speaker: Narrator
text: "That makes no sense at all. It shouldn't be inside the Mizizi forest. Why would it be here? Why would it do the exact same thing to you that it does to the canyon folk?!".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Where does it come from?"

speaker: Narrator
text: Britt asked.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Was it manufactured, or does it grow naturally?".

speaker: Narrator
text: "It isn't manufactured," Rill whispered.

speaker: Narrator
text: "It just grows.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Rill stepped over to the laboratory door, slid the heavy iron deadbolt shut, and turned to face the room. Only the four of them remained inside: Rill, Britt, Aggie, and Iggy, with Ignatius standing quietly near the ladder rungs.

speaker: Narrator
text: CHAPTER 10: WADI WATER.

speaker: Narrator
text: In the quiet of the locked laboratory, Rill leaned back against the steel door, wrapping her arms tightly around herself.

speaker: Britt
text: "I've been keeping this inside for so long," Rill confessed softly, looking between Britt, Aggie, and Iggy.

speaker: Narrator
text: "It's just so hard to talk about where I came from... the clan exchange scrubbed so much out of us, and I'm still trying to overcome that indoctrination every day. But I want to be honest with you.".

speaker: Narrator
text: She took a deep breath, her electric-blue hair falling across her brow.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I'm originally from a clan that called themselves the Wadi. We lived in the deep western canyon. Our ancestral spark—the thing that made our people special—was a sacred source of water. But for my entire childhood, the spring was dead. Just a few dry drips and trickles. We thought our entire civilization was dying out.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius stepped closer, his eyes wide with recognition.

speaker: Ignatious
text: "That's just like the Ash-Blood clan," Ignatius whispered.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Our magma springs went cold... we thought our whole people were going to go under.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Yes," Rill nodded, her voice thick with emotion.

speaker: Narrator
text: "It was the exact same thing. When I was chosen for the exchange, I left not even knowing if my family would survive. But in our canyon, there was a deep, hidden cave—one of the only places that stayed damp through the worst droughts. And that cave was where this glowing fungus grew. It needed that spring and should not have been able to grow anywhere else in the world. So for you to say that you've seen people suffering from these symptoms in the Mizizi forest... the only explanation is that something connected our lands in the ancient before-times.".

speaker: Ignatious
text: "The old turtles," Ignatius suggested.

speaker: Narrator
text: "The ancient network.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Maybe," Rill murmured.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I was never trusted with the deepest clan secrets because I was new. But I traveled through the mycelium network once... and it was terrifying.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "That's how we survived the arena storm!"

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius said proudly.

speaker: Britt
text: "Thanks to Britt and Aggie speaking to the roots, we didn't die in the forest.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Aggie chimed in shaking her head.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Talking to trees is different. There's the fungal network, which speaks to the living flora, and then there's the deep mycelium network, which carries the soul and allows physical travel across the network.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Rill turned back to the lab counter, flipping through stacks of parchment charts and botanical sketches. She pointed to a glass terrarium holding three small field mice, each showing the same distinct grey fungal decay along their spines.

speaker: Britt
text: "I don't love animal testing," Rill admitted quietly, "but when I realized what was happening to you, Britt, I panicked. I worked with Professor Ink using Harmony compounds to synthesize this stabilizer. This isn't natural to the forest. Someone brought it here.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Britt crossed her arms, her jaw tightening.

speaker: Narrator
text: "This substance wasn't found in the deep woods. I was infected right after we arrived in Harmony, down in a drainage ditch near the cliffside where we found an old cache containing a ten-year-old compass.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Rill went rigid.

speaker: Narrator
text: "A ten-year-old cache?! Has anyone else in your clan ever died from this condition?".

speaker: Britt
text: "Yes," Britt answered.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I can sort of remember... about ten people. Adventurers who left the forest to explore the outer world.".

speaker: Narrator
text: A chill settled over the room.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Ten people," Rill whispered.

speaker: Narrator
text: "All curious wanderers who left the forest... dying of a poison that exists in only one isolated canyon gorge.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius looked between them, scratching his head.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Wait... isn't dying supposed to be considered a natural, good thing in your clan philosophy?".

speaker: Ignatious
text: "Ignatius, read the room!"

speaker: Narrator
text: Rill hissed.

speaker: Narrator
text: "We are on an active investigation!".

speaker: Narrator
text: "No, think about it!"

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius insisted, stepping forward.

speaker: Narrator
text: "My people were dying out, then we connected with Harmony, and suddenly our magma erupted with life! Your clan revered death and balance, and now that you've connected with Harmony, you're finding more death and disease! Doesn't the timeline seem suspicious?".

speaker: Britt
text: "We do not worship death," Brittt corrected fiercely.

speaker: Narrator
text: "We acknowledge that death is an inevitable truth of the world, and that balance between growth and decay must be respected. But the last time this illness appeared among the Mizizi was ten years ago—long before Captain Vane ever discovered our valley, and long before the Harmony cartographers arrived!".

speaker: Ignatious
text: "Which means there is a third, unknown variable at play," Ignatius concluded.

speaker: Britt
text: "Exactly," Rill said. She picked up the neon-purple vial, pressing it gently into Britt's hands.

speaker: Britt
text: "I don't have all the answers yet, Britt. But I know for a fact that if you don't drink this, you won't survive the fortnight.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Britt hesitated, staring down at the swirling tonic.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Intervening like this... it feels like interrupting the natural path. Is this supposed to happen?".

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius placed a warm, steady hand on Britt's shoulder, his voice dropping to a sincere, earnest cadence.

speaker: Ignatious
text: "Britt, hear me out," Ignatius said gently.

speaker: Narrator
text: "This isn't an interruption of nature. This medicine was made from natural waters, synthesized so that you can stay alive and save your people. You are a core part of this squad. We need you for whatever is coming next. Nobody in this room wants to watch you die—and I genuinely do not believe it is your time to go.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Britt looked up, meeting Ignatius's warm, fiery eyes, then glanced at Aggie and Iggy's supportive faces.

speaker: Britt
text: "That's not for you to decide," Britt murmured softly.

speaker: Ignatious
text: "You're right," Ignatius smiled warmly.

speaker: Narrator
text: "It's for you to decide.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Britt nodded. Without another word, she popped the cork, tipped the glass vial back, and drank the shimmering purple tonic in a single long gulp.

speaker: Narrator
text: Rill held her breath, leaning forward.

speaker: Narrator
text: "How does it taste?".

speaker: Narrator
text: Britt smacked her lips, blinking in surprise.

speaker: Narrator
text: "It... honestly tastes like Gatorade.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Gatorade!"

speaker: Narrator
text: Rill laughed with overwhelming relief, slumping against the counter.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Thank the Water."

speaker: Narrator
text: She wiped a bead of sweat from her forehead and smiled.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Okay. Now... onto the next problem.".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: Back up in the operations room, instead of following the squad into the lab, Lomi had ambled toward the iron spiral staircase leading up to the open-air observation bridge, eager to take in his very first sight of the world beyond the city walls.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: High atop the walker Elijah, the open observation bridge was constructed from polished bamboo struts, brass instrumentation, and reinforced glass.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: From this elevated vantage, the world unfolded into an endless, emerald expanse of rolling savanna grassland.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: Far to the south, smudged against the pale morning horizon, the dark, colossal wall of the ancient Mizizi forest stretched for eighty miles—only the outer perimeter of their true destination.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: Up in the pilot's cradle at the forward helm sat a small, sharp-featured goblin driver, his clawed hands flicking brass toggle switches with bored, practiced efficiency. Standing beside the navigation console was Professor Ink, her sharp eyes studying the distant horizon.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: Ambling over to the helm with an easy mechanic's slouch, Lomi leaned on the brass railing.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "So... how hard is a beauty like this to drive?"

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi asked casually.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: The goblin pilot didn't even turn his head. Reaching over with a clawed thumb, he hammered a red locking lever that set the mechanical legs on a fixed, dead-straight trajectory.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "A lot harder when you don't have idiots asking questions," the goblin grunted flatly.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Buzz off.".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Fair enough," Lomi chuckled, leaning against the navigation console.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "I'm Lomi. Just a harbor mechanic taking in the view. Really beautiful work on these suspension gyros, by the way.".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi continuing to chat despite the tone of the driver, continued, "First time out of Vumbua, so I just thought I'd come up and take in the surroundings. It's beautiful out here.".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: The goblin rolled his eyes, turning back to his dials.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Buzz off, man.".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: Unbothered by the feisty driver, Lomi looked out over the open savanna. Ahead in the tall grass, a narrow, razor-sharp wake parted the green blades like a miniature bow wave—an arrow of disturbance knifing straight across the plains. Every few seconds, the dark, glistening ridge of a massive shell surfaced before submerging beneath the grass.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: Intrigued, Lomi studied the glowing acoustic holographic map projecting above the dashboard. The primary heading was plotted in crisp gold light across flat terrain. Looking back outside and comparing to the gauge Lomi noticed that the line the tortoise was cutting through the tall grass was running a degree or two off the walker's path. As he watched the tortoise quickly redirected, matching the heading of the Elijah, before twitching and snapping back it's off-axis trajectory like a beating heart signalling for attention. As it did, the map briefly showed a blip as if warning of a collission, before vanishing.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi tapped the display console, nudging the goblin pilot.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Hey... do you see what the turtle is doing on that acoustic track?".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: The goblin squinted over the high brass dashboard, grimacing.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "I can't see over the damn dash, and I don't care to try. I follow the gold arrow. That's my job.".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi turned to Professor Ink, who was watching him with keen, analytical curiosity.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Professor," Lomi said, pointing to the shimmering teal trace.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Is that stutter on the projection a navigational glitch? Watch it for a second.".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: Professor Ink leaned over the console, her dark eyes narrowing.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "That is not a projection anomaly. That trace is tracking the acoustic resonance of the creature moving through the savanna."

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: She paused, her breath catching as she stared at the glass.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Wait... what did you just say about a turtle?".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "The magic turtle," Lomi replied calmly.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: Professor Ink went utterly rigid.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "I have heard about this turtle twice now....Interesting..."

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: Ink murmured, her eyes darting back to the plains. She gestured excitedly toward the parting grass.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Tell me what you are seeing! This line here in the grass... it's a turtle running at... well it is an absurdly fast turtle".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: " I mean, it's a magic turtle," Lomi chuckled, leaning against the brass rail. " So it's probably pretty quivck. Keep looking at it, Professor. Keep your eyes locked on the wake in the grass.".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "It is off by two degrees," Ink noted sharply, her analytical mind seizing on the discrepancy.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Why?".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "That's the question," Lomi smiled.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "And it's about to snap in front of us. Just wait.".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: Ahead in the grass, the green wake twitched and snapped abruptly back match the Elijah's vector - with the small map showing it's dot, before adjusting to it's original heading again, diverging from the Elijah.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: Ink gasped softly.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "What was that? Why did it do that? Did you tell it to do that?".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "No, I didn't," Lomi answered, shaking his head.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "I just wanted to make sure you were seeing what I was seeing".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "That vector is to a different part of the forest," Ink murmured in rising wonder.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "That is to the center. That is not where the clans live.".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "I think we need to adjust our heading," Lomi said firmly.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "A big ask from a harbor mechanic," Ink challenged, raising an eyebrow.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi flashed a confident grin.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Hey... let me ask you something, Professor. Are you feeling lucky?".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: Professor Ink, looked a Lomi for a moment before decisively turning to the helm.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Adjust heading. Two degrees south-southwest.".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: The goblin pilot turned around in his chair, glaring in complete disbelief.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Are you seriously going to listen to this guy?!"

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: the goblin shouted.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "He just walked up here and started talking about a magic turtle running through the grass!".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Set two degrees," Professor Ink commanded crisply.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Lock the heading.".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: The goblin grumbled, spinning the primary brass rudder until the walker's mechanical gait swung two degrees to port, aligning perfectly with the tortoise's wake.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: Professor Ink pulled a small leather notepad from her vest, furiously scribbling notes.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Lomi... I am about to look away from the savanna. Give me forty seconds, then ask me why we altered course.".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Should I act angry?"

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi asked with a grin.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Like you made a mistake?".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "No," Ink said seriously.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Just instruct me to read my notes.".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: She turned her back to the panoramic windows, staring fixedly at the blank mahogany bulkhead. Thirty seconds passed in dead silence. Forty seconds. Ink blinked, shook her head slightly, and turned back to Lomi with a polite, puzzled smile.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Ah, Lomi. You were asking about our destination coordinates?".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Doc," Lomi said without missing a beat, "we just drifted off the primary course. What are you doing?".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: Professor Ink frowned in sudden alarm, looking at the helm.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "I didn't alter the course... you told me to alter course by two degrees! But why did I—" She stopped, her voice faltering as she stared into the terrifying blank space in her own memory.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Check your notepad, Professor," Lomi told her gently.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Make sure you didn't mess something up.".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: Ink flipped open the notebook, reading her own frantic handwriting: Don't look at turtle. Cadets can see turtle. Follow turtle.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: She let out a long, shuddering breath, closing the book.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Lomi... how many people aboard this vessel can maintain continuous visual tracking on that creature?".

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "At least seven of us," Lomi answered.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "Then we institute a permanent watch rotation," Professor Ink ordered.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "There must be one cadet stationed on this bridge at all times, keeping their eyes locked on the grass so the heading never drifts."

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: She moved toward the ladder hatch.

chapter: CHAPTER 11: THE HEARTBEAT IN THE GRASS
speaker: Narrator
text: "I must confer with the research lab immediately.".

speaker: Narrator
text: CHAPTER 12: THE FORGETFULNESS & THE CLANS.

speaker: Narrator
text: Professor Ink dropped down the ladder into the lower laboratory barge, her mind racing faster than her feet could move.

speaker: Britt
text: "Did Britt receive the stabilizer?"

speaker: Narrator
text: Ink asked immediately, scanning the room.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Is she cured?".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Not cured," Rill answered from the counter.

speaker: Narrator
text: "The progression has been delayed.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Delayed is good," Professor Ink breathed, steadying herself. She turned to the squad, her eyes shining with manic scientific excitement.

speaker: Narrator
text: "We have established an unprecedented cognitive phenomenon. Every person in this room can see the Spirit Tortoise—what no one outside our party can do is retain the memory of having seen it! Out in the savanna, the moment your gaze leaves the creature, the entity completely erases its existence from your mind!".

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius stepped into the center of the lab, holding up both hands.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Hold on, hold on. Are you saying we're the only ones in the entire empire who can actually see the damn turtle?!".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Not the only ones who can see it," Ink clarified.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Anyone can see it when looking directly at it. The trick is that breaking visual contact erases the memory from the observer's mind.".

speaker: Britt
text: "It makes people forget," Britt whispered, her eyes wide as the ancient lore pieces aligned.

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius looked around the room.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Raise your hand if you remember the turtle right now.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Every hand in the room went up—except Rill's, who wavered awkwardly.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I remember talking about turtles... sort of," Rill muttered, her brow furrowing in frustration.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Like a dream slipping away.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Professor Ink held up her leather notepad.

speaker: Britt
text: "I had originally planned to navigate Elijah straight to the Mizizi clan to consult your clan elders regarding the node synchronization failure. But every instinct demands we follow this tortoise instead. Britt... what does your clan lore say about these entities?".

speaker: Britt
text: "Our people live alongside the tortoises," Britt explained softly, coming to a decision in her mind to finally trust Professor Ink and the scholars, realizing that there was something that needed to be solved here, "The tradition has always been to maintain careful distance and never interfere with their path. But this creature approached us. It sought us out.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Is there a formal law governing interaction?"

speaker: Narrator
text: Ink pressed.

speaker: Britt
text: "Not a written law," Britt said.

speaker: Narrator
text: "A social norm passed down through generations: leave them be. Do not look at them, do not touch them, and never follow them.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "And you looked at it," Professor Ink observed sharply.

speaker: Narrator
text: "And Rill said you touched it last night in the forest. And what happened?".

speaker: Pip
text: "Pip was pulled inside its memory space," Britt revealed, glancing at Aggie.

speaker: Narrator
text: "And when we touched it, we witnessed ancient memories of our people—wanderers who asked questions and died from the exact same illness spreading on my skin.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Professor Ink listened with rapt attention, nodding solemnly.

speaker: Professor Kante
text: "This aligns with Professor Kante's working thesis. Harmony's inability to synchronize with the Mizizi is rooted in a cultural taboo that your ancestors were explicitly forbidden to break. By breaking that social norm, you may have given us a hint on why we cannot form a node connection with the Mizizi.".

speaker: Narrator
text: She paced across the laboratory deck, looking at each of the cadets in turn, her analytical mind whirring to connect the pieces.

speaker: Pip
text: "And this entity deliberately selected individuals from our camp. It stopped for Zephyr, which of course we know she is.. special. But it also stopped for Pip and Bramble you say, why?".

speaker: Narrator
text: Ink turned toward Britt.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Do you recognize which clans are represented here?".

speaker: Narrator
text: Britt closed her eyes. In the quiet darkness behind his eyelids, the memory unlocked by the tortoise surfaced with crystal clarity—faces from the Great Clan Exchange that she had never been able to recall before.

speaker: Britt
text: "I remember them now," Britt said, opening his eyes and looking straight at Saffron and Iggy.

speaker: Iggy
text: "There was an Earthkin woman who looked just like Iggy... and a pale, quiet scholar who carried the exact high-browed features of Saffron.".

speaker: Pip
text: Professor Ink's eyes widened in realization, "Saffron was with Pip and Bramble, yes? Rill please go find Saffron and bring her here immediately".

speaker: Narrator
text: CHAPTER 13: THE SIXTH CLAN.

speaker: Narrator
text: Rill returned from the upper decks leading Saffron by the hand. The pale Renali scholar's eyes were wide with apprehension, clutching her sketching pad against her chest as if the bustling laboratory were full of hungry predators.

speaker: Narrator
text: Professor Ink stepped forward, softening her posture.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Saffron... can you tell us where your people originate?".

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius nudged Iggy with an elbow.

speaker: Iggy
text: "Hey, Iggy—this is your specialty. Help her out.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Iggy took a deliberate step backward, pulling his collar up.

speaker: Narrator
text: "No. My specialty is the exact opposite of this.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Professor Ink knelt slightly before Saffron, speaking with gentle urgency.

speaker: Narrator
text: "It is vital to our expedition that we understand your origin. Are you from the central plains of Harmony?".

speaker: Narrator
text: Saffron shook her head slowly, keeping her lips pressed tight.

speaker: Aggie
text: "She doesn't speak," Aggie offered quietly from the examination table.

speaker: Narrator
text: "She draws.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Do you have your sketchbook?"

speaker: Narrator
text: Ink asked gently.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Could you draw your home for us?".

speaker: Narrator
text: Saffron hesitated, looking around at the circle of cadets. Seeing Aggie and Britt nod encouragingly, she pulled a piece of charcoal from her pocket and set her pad on the counter. With swift, elegant strokes, Saffron sketched a breathtaking landmass: an enormous, jagged mountain island floating entirely suspended in mid-air above the sea, completely disconnected from the earth below.

speaker: Narrator
text: The room went completely silent as everyone stared at the impossible floating island.

speaker: Narrator
text: Watching Saffron's sketch unlocked something deep within Iggy. Reaching onto the workbench, the little dirt-kin creature grabbed a quill, pulled a scrap of parchment toward him with a map of Vumbua, and without a single word, drew a heavy arrow plunging straight down through dark water to the absolute bedrock floor of the deep ocean.

speaker: Narrator
text: Professor Ink studied both sketches, counting the clans on her fingers with rising awe.

speaker: Narrator
text: "The Spirit Tortoise has deliberately assembled six distinct clan lineages aboard this vessel," Professor Ink declared softly.

speaker: Ignatious
text: "Zephyr representing the Storm-Callers; Ignatius from the Ash-Blood flame; Iggy from this place below the waves; Britt and Aggie from the Mizizi roots; Saffron from what appear to be floating islands; and Rill representing the ancient Wadi water.".

speaker: Narrator
text: She looked up at the cadets, her determination absolute.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I do not yet know what awaits us in the deep forest, but this creature is operating under an ancient, deliberate design. And that is more than reason enough to follow it.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Britt stood up from the stool, rolling her shoulders.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I'll help Lomi take the first watch on the bridge to keep our eyes locked on its path.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Let's move," Professor Ink commanded.

speaker: Narrator
text: CHAPTER 14: THE OLD GROWTH.

speaker: Narrator
text: For two days, the walker Elijah galloped southward across the plains, maintaining a strict watch rotation at the bridge helm so that no cadet ever broke visual contact with Mwaza-Kasa's wake in the grass.

speaker: Narrator
text: On the third morning, the savanna gave way to towering ancient timbers. The petrified canopy thickened into an impenetrable labyrinth of colossal moss-draped trunks, forcing Elijah to grind to a halt at the edge of the forbidden old growth. The expedition disembarked onto the damp loam, continuing on foot into territory that Mizizi elders had explicitly forbidden their youth from ever entering.

speaker: Narrator
text: At the center of a wide, mist-shrouded clearing stood the largest living organism any of them had ever witnessed—a colossal, ancient primordial tree whose petrified roots coiled across the clearing like sleeping dragons.

speaker: Narrator
text: Encircling the base of the massive trunk was a thirty-foot ring of dense, glowing neon-green fungus—the exact lethal organism Rill had identified from the canyon caves, and that Britt had stumbled across in her explorations.

speaker: Narrator
text: Rill gasped in pure horror, stumbling back.

speaker: Narrator
text: "They're cultivating it..."

speaker: Narrator
text: Rill breathed in terrified disbelief.

speaker: Narrator
text: "How is that even possible?!".

speaker: Narrator
text: Mwaza-Kasa crawled steadily to the edge of the clearing, turned back to meet the gaze of each member of the party, and then waddled straight into the ring of lethal fungus. Reaching the ancient bark, the giant Spirit Tortoise pressed its front limb against the wood—and collapsed motionless to the earth.

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius cried out in alarm, jumping forward.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Don't touch that! Did the turtle just die?!".

speaker: Narrator
text: CHAPTER 14: EIGHT VIALS.

speaker: Narrator
text: Trying to learn more about her surroundings, Aggie walked to an adjacent sentinel tree on the edge of the clearing, placing her palms against its bark to commune with the roots. But the wood remained cold, silent, and petrified - there was no life inside the bark of the trees surrounding the grove, they were solid stone.

speaker: Narrator
text: Rill unslung her satchel, stepping up to the perimeter.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I have eight vials of stabilizing antidote," Rill announced firmly.

speaker: Narrator
text: "It won't cure us permanently, but it gives us time. If we are going to touch that tree and uncover what happened here... we take the draught together.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Iggy didn't wait to be invited.

speaker: Narrator
text: Grabbing a vial and knocking it back, he pulled his heavy trench coat tight around his dirt-kin frame, then marched straight through the thirty-foot perimeter of glowing fungal spores. The toxic dust swirled around him as he reached the fallen tortoise, kneeling beside its shell, he touched the trunk and also fell asleep.

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius blinked, looking around the clearing in confusion.

speaker: Iggy
text: "Where'd Iggy go? Wait—did he just fall asleep immediately?".

speaker: Narrator
text: Before anyone could answer, Zephyr snatched a vial of her own, vaulted over the roots, and charged headlong through the fungal mist to slap her palm flat against the petrified trunk, dropping into the moss beside Iggy a heartbeat later.

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius threw his hands in the air, embers flaring wildly at his cuffs.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Fuck, I better go," he groaned.

speaker: Iggy
text: "Iggy is going to be so pissed that Zephyr followed him in there!".

speaker: Narrator
text: Britt stepped forward, rolling her shoulders and staring down at the vials in Rill's hands. Her dreadlocks of living root shifted with quiet resolve.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I'm going too," she said firmly.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I already carry the infection anyway, so I might as well.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Professor Ink adjusted her brass spectacles, stepping forward to study the glowing veins pulsing beneath the bark.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I believe one representative from each of the clans should take a vial," the professor observed.

speaker: Narrator
text: "And perhaps two others—those who feel the deepest resonance with the network—should join them.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Rill nodded in quiet agreement.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Wherever this leads, we need to go together. It shouldn't be me—I don't possess a connection to the Mizizi network. But two non-clansmen who are willing to take the risk could step forward.".

speaker: Pip
text: Safrron who was looking at Professor Ink shaking her head near-panic, caught the attention of Pip, "Saffron, why are you shaking your head?"

speaker: Narrator
text: Pip demanded, bouncing on her heels.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Are you a clan member? Saffron? Saffron! That's SO COOL WHY DIDN'T YOU TELL US?!".

speaker: Pip
text: "Pip, let her be," Bramble rumbled softly, extending a vine to gently tug the excitable pixie back.

speaker: Narrator
text: Meeting the calm, confident and supportive gaze of Bramble, Saffrons panic was replaced with a hint of shame. then determination. She nodded before reaching to grab a vial of her own from Rill and stepped up to lay her slender fingers against the living wood, collapsing gently into the moss.

speaker: Narrator
text: Next, Lomi pushed his flat cap back, stepping out from the shadow of the stone terrace.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I'll take one, Rill" he said simply, "if you're willing.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Makes sense to me, Lomi," Rill replied, extending a vial toward him.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi took the glass cylinder, popped the stopper, and downed the bitter draught in a single gulp. He grimaced then chased the taste a drag of Grease he pulled from a flask in his pocket, before walking calmly to the tree and placing his bare hand against the bark. His knees folded beneath him as the ancient resonance pulled him under.

speaker: Narrator
text: That left only a single open place.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lucky and Pip stepped forward at the exact same instant, stopping inches apart and glaring at each other.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lucky crossed his arms, his confident smile wavering slightly as he eyed the ominous, pulsing spores.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Look... it just kind of feels like if one of us is going to get through this without a scratch, it's probably going to be me.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Pip planted her tiny boots into the moss and jabbed a fierce finger at her own chest.

speaker: Narrator
text: "No, dude! They like me way more than you!".

speaker: Narrator
text: Lucky hesitated, looking between the colossal petrified tree and the stubborn pixie. Muttering under his breath, "Maybe I shouldnt bring my so -called luck into this."

speaker: Pip
text: he took a step back, and gave Pip a shrug, sweeping an arm toward the oak he said out loud, " You know what? You're right. Be my guest.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Pip puffed her chest in triumph—and then froze.

speaker: Narrator
text: Her giant eyes went wide with sudden, horrified realization.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Oh shit..."

speaker: Narrator
text: she squeaked, her voice climbing an octave.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Did I just volunteer myself?!".

speaker: Narrator
text: She whipped around toward Rill, waving both hands in desperate agitation.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Quick before a change my mind. Give me! Give me!".

speaker: Narrator
text: Snatching the final vial, Pip downed the liquid, closed her eyes, and sprinted full speed through the glowing spore cloud, and slammed her forehead with a resounding thwack straight into the petrified trunk—knocking herself out cold as she tumbled into a heap on the moss.

speaker: Narrator
text: CHAPTER 15: THE ANCESTRAL VISION.

speaker: Narrator
text: As each of the clan membners and their firends touched petrified wood, the clearing at Center Grove dissolved. One by one - they entered the same series of visions, though they would not know this until they came out the other side.

speaker: Narrator
text: The air did not merely blur—it fractured. Space unfolded like ancient parchment, and the world of mud, canvas tents, and iron machinery was torn away in a blinding rush of luminous teal Aether.

speaker: Narrator
text: It was not a dream, nor was it a simple illusion cast upon the mind. It felt like stepping into the memory of a stranger—seeing through eyes that had turned to dust a thousand years before, feeling the secondhand warmth of fires long extinguished, hearing the voices of a forgotten age. The vision belonged to Mwaza-Kasa, stored within the quiet, immortal shell of the Spirit Tortoise. It did not invite them in as participants. It allowed them to witness as the tortoise had always witnessed—patient, ancient, observant, and utterly without judgement.

speaker: Narrator
text: An each in their own mind, they watched as outside observers peering into secondhand memory. They saw the living reality of people, places, and sparks as they unfolded across time.

speaker: Narrator
text: ACT I: THE FIRST UNION.

speaker: Narrator
text: The world was vast, wild, and fragmented into silence. On a jet-black volcanic sand beach under a heavy blanket of tropical sea mist, two primitive peoples lived in absolute isolation, separated by hostile terrain.

speaker: Narrator
text: On the left, shivering beneath simple structures build under the broad, dripping leaves of a dense, cold rainforest, huddled the early root-dwellers—turtle-fungus humanoids with dark scaled skin, clutching woven ivy shawls around their lumpy shells, living in damp misery without the warmth of fire. On the right, silhouetted against roaring lava vents and glowing magma crags, huddled the smoldering warriors of the volcanic peaks—their dark obsidian skin dusted with soot, literal crowns of orange flame burning from their scalps, possessing raw elemental heat but devoid of architecture, shifting unfomrtably as they tried to sleep no the bare volcanic rock.

speaker: Narrator
text: Between them lay the neutral ground of wet black sand, where the turquoise tide crashed indifferently.

speaker: Narrator
text: From the forest edge stepped a tall, regal turtle-kin elder, leaning on a staff of petrified ironbark. From the volcanic crags stepped a towering warrior chieftain in beaten bronze scale armor, embers smoldering in his yellow-orange eyes.

speaker: Narrator
text: They possessed no shared language. Neither knew a single word the other spoke.

speaker: Narrator
text: Standing on the wet black sand, knowing no words, each leader chose to draw the living spark of their people into the earth.

speaker: Narrator
text: The smoldering warrior knelt, holding a glowing shard of volcanic glass, and seared a smooth, stepped sun-spire fire arc into the jet-black sand. The root-kin elder stepped forward, raised his petrified staff, and struck it straight through the center of the arc, carving a deep, vertical root-ladder spine.

speaker: Narrator
text: A connection was born. The first union between clans.

speaker: Narrator
text: The meeting unleashed an explosive era of cultural and physical creation. The ancient world did not build cold, mechanical engines or combust fossil fuels; their technology was an organic, elemental marvel powered by their living sparks.

speaker: Narrator
text: Root woodcraft and volcanic thermal engineering combined. Smiths and wood-weavers worked side by side, fitting glowing bronze heat conduits through living ironbark timber frames, creating the comfortable, climate-controlled homes for the clans. Above every doorway, the combined two-stroke petroglyph mandala was deeply chiseled into the lintel. Inside the warm, glowing rooms, the amber light of core-fire lamps cast shadow puppets across polished timber walls, where families of both clans sat together, laughing in the initial joy of mutual discovery.

speaker: Narrator
text: And one after another, as the joined clans discovered next. The Deep, the Storm, the Air, and the Water, connections were formed, and an empire began to grow.

speaker: Narrator
text: ACT II: THE SYNERGISTIC MESH OF SPARKS.<break time="1.4s"/> The web expanded, and with every clan that joined the union, the elemental sparks did not merely coexist—they interlocked, multiplying one another's capabilities and enabling each civilization to achieve what had once been physically impossible.

speaker: Narrator
text: In the dark ocean caverns where waves crashed against towering basalt cliffs, the subterranean clay-kin huddled on cold ledges. Short, rounded humanoids of packed brown clay and smooth stone, wearing dark green seaweed robes pinned with polished silver pauldrons, they were master masons who longed to build cities in the ocean depths, but could never survive the freezing cold or the crushing pressure of the abyss.

speaker: Narrator
text: The alliance provided the key. The sky-dwellers' mastery over atmospheric air currents and barometric pressure allowed the clay-kin to regulate the pressure inside deep-sea habitats, creating breathable, climate-controlled stone domes beneath the waves. Combined with flexible root-wood scaffolding and volcanic thermal bronze conduits, the clay-kin constructed colossal, luminous cities inside subterranean ocean caves. Bioluminescent teal root-lamps lit stone walkways, while heated water channels flowed past carved basalt colonnades.

speaker: Narrator
text: And at the center of the entire empire stood the root-kin archivists. The living petrified oak forests served as the grand archive of the world. Archivist scholars meticulously encoded and preserved the complex resonance formulas in the living tree bark, teaching every clan how to weave their elemental sparks together into harmonious, living circuits.

speaker: Narrator
text: In the sandstone canyons, the canyon-dwellers built terraced cliffside gardens fed by volcanic thermal warmth, subterranean mineral soil, and root-kin botanical design. High above in the heavens, the sky-dwellers transformed their frozen floating sky-isles into glorious terraced step-ziggurats and crystal spires suspended on heavy copper cables, their giant biological dragonflies pulling elegant wooden sky-chariots between landing pads.

speaker: Narrator
text: Atop the central sky-altar, a graceful sky-scholar in flowing purple silk placed a glowing turquoise crystal sphere into the completed mandala plate.

speaker: Narrator
text: "The circle is woven!" she cried as golden light flared across the ziggurat.

speaker: Narrator
text: "One Mandala!" the elders answered in unison. "One Empire!".

speaker: Narrator
text: ACT III: THE GOLDEN APEX & THE COMFORTABLE ROT.<break time="1.4s"/> For a golden age, there was unmatched, effortless prosperity.

speaker: Narrator
text: The Grand Forum of the Sun-Spire stood as the pinnacle of achievement: colossal white marble plazas framed by living petrified oak towers that reached toward the clouds. Iridescent biological dragonflies glided through azure skies in graceful arcs. The central petroglyph mandala on the imperial spire glowed with unbroken, radiant teal light.

speaker: Narrator
text: From the forum balcony, the Empress of the Golden Age addressed the multitudes: "People of the Five Domains! As long as our connection endures, this golden age will never end!".

speaker: Narrator
text: And that was the lie that doomed them.

speaker: Narrator
text: Generations passed in effortless luxury. Surrounded by boundless abundance, society stopped challenging itself. Because survival required zero effort, genuine curiosity and discovery ground to a complete halt.

speaker: Narrator
text: Citizens reclined lazily on silk couches in the grand plazas, eating fruit and ignoring hairline fractures in the conduits. Clan boundaries blurred into a comfortable, homogenized mediocrity. At council tables, leaders waved away new ventures with a complacent shrug: "So much effort to do new things... why bother? We already have everything we could ever need right here.".

speaker: Narrator
text: In the high Imperial Observatory, a colossal copper-and-stone floor mosaic world map of Vumbua spanned the chamber. A central astrolabe cast shifting seasonal shadows across the floor—spring blossom giving way to summer sun, autumn leaves falling across the stone, winter frost coating the arched windows.

speaker: Narrator
text: Generations walked indifferently over the map, never once looking out toward the uncharted horizons.

speaker: Narrator
text: An aging architect in brass spectacles looked down at the dust gathering on the map's outer edges.

speaker: Narrator
text: "My Empress..." the architect murmured, shaking his head. "The surveyors turned back at the borders. Not because they feared the Dark Undone... but because they saw exploration as pointless effort. They simply said we have enough right here.".

speaker: Narrator
text: The Empress looked at her fading silk robes, her voice hollow with grief. "We lied to ourselves. Resting on our successes was our decay.".

speaker: Narrator
text: ACT IV: THE BREAKDOWN & THE REGRESSION OF WAR.<break time="1.4s"/> Because the people refused to grow or strive, the living elemental sparks began to suffocate.

speaker: Narrator
text: The physical infrastructure of the empire began to fracture. In the deep sea habitats, the atmospheric pressure seals maintained by sky-air currents failed, and crushing ocean water violently shattered the clay-kin glass domes. In the skies, giant biological dragonflies—overloaded with luxury cargo and heavy passenger cabins—strained and flipped in mid-air, plunging into the cloud sea. Atop the basalt step-pyramids, unmaintained cooling channels ran dry, and lightning conductors exploded under storm strikes, showering the streets in fire and masonry.

speaker: Narrator
text: The time of abundance was over.

speaker: Narrator
text: Panic, famine, and accusation spread like wildfire. A toxic belief took root across the five domains: War is the answer. War will force an evolution. War will reignite the dying sparks! So the clans went to war.

speaker: Narrator
text: All five domains clashed across their once-glorious cities in a catastrophic grand melee. But the tragedy deepened with every battle: the most advanced weapons were compound multi-spark constructs—magma cannons that required volcanic fire channeled through canyon cooling conduits; lightning ballistas that required tempest voltage focused through barometric air barrels; hydraulic pressure rams that required subterranean masonry powered by root tension.

speaker: Narrator
text: As cross-clan harmony shattered and the individual sparks lost power, every compound weapon failed completely. Magma cannons sputtered into cold slag.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lightning-arc ballistas cracked and shorted out. Hydraulic rams seized.

speaker: Narrator
text: The war tragically regressed into crude, primitive medieval butchery. Soldiers who had once commanded living elemental physics were forced to slaughter one another with crude iron swords, wooden spears, and heavy siege catapults.

speaker: Narrator
text: Yet no matter how much blood was spilled, the sparks did not return. The sparks had continued to decay, suffocating and growing dimmer with every passing generation that clung to past glories. Without them, absolute extinction loomed.

speaker: Narrator
text: ACT V: THE SPARK-SOUL TRUTH & THE GOLDILOCKS CONDUIT.<break time="1.4s"/> While the surface world tore itself apart, the cross-clan council of scholars met in a secret subterranean stone vault beneath the ancient roots.

speaker: Narrator
text: The scholars gathered in the dim candlelight were dying, their physical frames bearing the horrifying marks of their failing sparks. Across the stone table, a volcanic ember scholar strained with all his might just to coax a faint, pathetic spark from his hair. Beside him, a root-kin archivist clutched his temples in agonizing pain, suffering catatonic seizures whenever he attempted to recall memories from five years past. A canyon scholar stared in hollow despair at a cracked, bone-dry clay water vessel, while a sky-dweller struggled simply to stir a breath of air in the stifling chamber.

speaker: Narrator
text: A root-kin spore-scholar unrolled a glowing parchment scroll depicting living roots intertwined with human heart-sparks, his voice trembling with terrible certainty.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Each civilization's elemental spark is not a tool," the scholar revealed. "It is an integral part of our soul. As the decay intensified, it began consuming the sparks. When the spark truly dies... it will take our souls with it. We will not survive.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Silence fell over the vault.

speaker: Narrator
text: The spore-scholar lifted a small dual-chambered glass conduit filled with a tiny, trickling stream of glowing teal sand.

speaker: Narrator
text: "The war purged our requirement to sustain a large population," the scholar explained softly. "We must find a way to live off the very little we have left, without upsetting the delicate balance. We do not have enough will left to create a massive new connection that could save us, and if we grow with what we have the decayed network will collapse, and it will take us with it. But if we establish The Exchange—a tiny, controlled conduit that trades just enough connection between our peoples—it will move just enough resonance to keep our soul-sparks alive in isolation, until a new generation learns how to truly grow.".

speaker: Narrator
text: ACT VI: THE WANTILA ROOT & THE MEMORY PURGE.<break time="1.4s"/> The decision was sealed in sorrow.

speaker: Narrator
text: At the perimeter of the ancient forest, a multi-clan coalition gathered to fell the great petrified timber canopy. Subterranean masons swung heavy iron axes, volcanic warriors scorched trunks with forge torches, canyon dwellers pulled two-man crosscut saws, and sky dwellers hauled heavy ropes. Colossal petrified trunks crashed into the dust, leaving a desolate wasteland of stumps.

speaker: Narrator
text: An ember-kin scholar placed a comforting hand on the shoulder of a weeping root-kin archivist.

speaker: Narrator
text: "You know these memories and this bark must die," the ember scholar said gently.

speaker: Narrator
text: "If they remain, your children will remember what was lost. They will seek it out before they are ready—and collapse the fragile circuit, bringing doom upon us all.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "We must at least keep the oldest grove," the root archivist wept, "or our spark will die anyway.".

speaker: Narrator
text: To ensure no curious wanderer ever stumbled upon the remaining anchor, a canyon scholar planted a glowing, toxic-green root around the base of the central petrified oak in Center Grove: the Wantila root.

speaker: Narrator
text: "We who dwell in the canyons will plant this Wantila root," the canyon scholar whispered somberly. "It will splatter invisibly upon any who draw near, poisoning them slowly and painlessly. I will teach your elders how to tend it...

speaker: Narrator
text: but I will never teach you how to cure it. That knowledge must stay with the Wadi to protect us all.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "We will teach our youth to treat this grove as a taboo of death," the root archivist answered, lowering his head. "If they will not listen, it is better that one curious wanderer die than our entire people perish. May the future forgive what we have unleashed upon them.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Deep beneath the surface, in the subterranean root conduits, root-kin archivists pressed glowing cyan mycelium strands against their temples. A massive wave of dark, memory-purging psychic energy pulsed through the root network, systematically wiping every memory of the grand empire, the golden age, and the other clans from the minds of the populace.

speaker: Narrator
text: In the vision's final, breathtaking instant, five hands—turtle-kin, ember-kin, clay-kin, tempest-kin, and sky-kin—placed their clan rings onto the central stone pact tablet.

speaker: Narrator
text: The central spire flame died. The subterranean vault shattered in a deafening acoustic rupture, tearing space into a swirling vortex of high-frequency teal energy.

speaker: Narrator
text: And as the portal spun, the ancient Spirit Tortoise itself turned its massive head within the river of memory. Its glowing golden-teal eyes met the gazes of the eleven travelers directly, conveying the profound truth across the millennia: it had carried and guarded these forbidden memories through the long dark, keeping the truth alive in its living shell until a generation arrived that was ready to learn, connect, and grow again.

speaker: Narrator
text: CHAPTER 16: MOMENTUM IS LIFE.

speaker: Narrator
text: Consciousness snapped back into their bodies like a bowstring released.

speaker: Narrator
text: The damp forest floor. The twilight shadows of Center Grove. The ancient petrified oak, silent and colossal against the darkening sky.

speaker: Narrator
text: First to react, Pip rolled out of the thirty-foot ring of glowing fungus, shaking her head vigorously like a wet dog.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Whoa! That one was way cooler!"

speaker: Narrator
text: Pip shouted, sitting up in the moss with an undignified grin.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I am definitely getting out of this toxic stuff now, though!".

speaker: Narrator
text: Scrambling to her feet on the safe turf, Pip turned around and stopped dead in her tracks.

speaker: Narrator
text: In the center of the clearing, Mwaza-Kasa was rising.

speaker: Narrator
text: The colossal Spirit Tortoise pushed itself up from the damp soil, straightening its massive, pillar-like legs. As the ancient beast lifted its head into the twilight air, the surface of its immense carapace ignited with soft, radiant energy.

speaker: Narrator
text: Across the dark keratin scutes, ancient growth ridges and glowing veins of bioluminescent teal lichen formed a living, organic topographic map of the clan lands. Embedded directly into the natural shell plates, small pinpricks of runic light pulsed with elemental resonance, marking the forgotten strongholds of the lost world: the suspended sky-ziggurats of the Renali high above the cloud layer; the jagged mountain step-pyramids of the Fulgur; the terraced sandstone canyons of the Wadi; the fiery volcanic crags of the Ash-Blood; and, stretching across the deep oceanic basin, several distinct, glowing coordinates that marked the submerged cavern cities of the Trench-Kin.

speaker: Narrator
text: Iggy did not scramble away., he stood frozen at the base of the petrified tree, his trembling hands hovering in the air as if they belonged to a stranger. Water sloshed heavily against the curved glass of his oversized goggles as he stared at the glowing oceanic runes on the shell.

speaker: Narrator
text: As the rest of the group rose to their feet to gather around the map that Harmony could only dream of discovering.

speaker: Narrator
text: "My whole life is a lie..."

speaker: Narrator
text: Iggy whispered, his voice cracking with profound shock.

speaker: Narrator
text: He dropped to his knees beside the ancient tortoise. For centuries, the deepest law of the Earthkin had been silence, secrecy, and absolute isolation from the surface world. But as the memory of the dying empire burned in his mind, Iggy's jaw hardened. In an open, deliberate act of rebellion against centuries of clan tradition, Iggy raised a shaking, clay-stained finger and jabbed it firmly onto the glowing ocean coordinates on the shell.

speaker: Narrator
text: He looked up, meeting the eyes of the entire squad.

speaker: Iggy
text: "Right here," Iggy declared fiercely, his voice ringing across the quiet clearing.

speaker: Narrator
text: "This is where my people are. In the deep ocean trenches. That's where you'll find the Trench-Kin.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Beside him, Saffron knelt on the damp moss. Her slender, pale fingers traced slow, deliberate circles over the glowing cluster of runes marking her sky-ziggurat, committing the forgotten coordinates to memory.

speaker: Narrator
text: Iggy looked across the circle of cadets, his gaze resolute.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Isolation was never the answer.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi leaned back against the mossy stone terrace, pushing his flat cap back and exhaling a long, ragged breath. He looked across the clearing at the stunned squad.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Yeah. I just left Harmony for the first time today, so this is a lot to take in.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Professor Ink stepped back from the tree, the brass-bound resonant crystal device in her hand suddenly erupting into a high, chiming hum as teal and emerald light pulsed across its dials.

speaker: Narrator
text: "You've done it!"

speaker: Narrator
text: she gasped, her eyes wide behind her spectacles.

speaker: Narrator
text: "It's connected! What happened?".

speaker: Narrator
text: The communication stone in Lomi's pocket crackled to life, and Professor Kante's voice crackled through the crystal speaker in breathless excitement.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Professor Ink—there is a massive spike in the resonance! We're over the threshold!".

speaker: Narrator
text: Beneath their boots, the forest floor shuddered.

speaker: Narrator
text: Vibrant green shoots burst through the petrified soil—not uniformly, but surging outward in living waves from where the network had been touched most newly. Tiny petrified trees and golden moss erupted in thick clusters around Pip's still-breathing form, while fresh ivy sprouted directly between Lomi's heavy boots.

speaker: Narrator
text: Uhmm what's happening? shrieked Pip as the growth was particularly heave around her and Lomi.

speaker: Narrator
text: Rill stared at the racing growth in awe.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I think it just downloaded Harmony."

speaker: Narrator
text: Rill quickly filled in Professor Ink on what she had seen in the vision, with the whol egroup agreeing that is what they had seen too.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Knowledge!"

speaker: Narrator
text: Professor Ink exclaimed, scribbling frantically into her field journal with one hand while clutching the singing device with the other.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Your spark is knowledge! That's all it took—storing information here in the living network, exactly like we stored records of the clans in Harmony Prime! That's literally Harmony's information growing right now!".

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius crossed his arms, embers flickering at his cuffs as he stepped toward the trunk.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I mean, I think it's less about knowledge and more about cooperation, right?".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Cooperation yes, that forms the connection, but I think it's more specifc!"

speaker: Narrator
text: Professor Ink insisted, gesturing with her quill.

speaker: Narrator
text: "They called them sparks, and the specific spark of the Mizizi was storing memory!".

speaker: Ignatious
text: "Yeah," Ignatius conceded with a thoughtful nod.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Yeah, I guess so.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "And now it downloaded that information through people walking the network!"

speaker: Narrator
text: Professor Ink beamed.

speaker: Narrator
text: "For what I believe is the first time from anyone outside the Mizizi in centuries!".

speaker: Narrator
text: Pip, overcoming her initial fear of the growth, scrambled to her feet and went skipping through the clearing, tiny yellow flowers and wild ivy shoots blooming under her heels with every step she took. She skidded to a halt and looked down at her boots, then beamed at the towering plant-kin.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Brambies, Brambies! I'm like you! I'm making the plants grow, Bramble!".

speaker: Narrator
text: Are we at all concerned that the first knowledge stored about Harmony will be from Pip and Lomi? Val asked Lucky with a touch of concern.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Ehh I'm sure it will be fine.."

speaker: Narrator
text: Lucky replied while they both watched the halfling skip around the clearing.

speaker: Narrator
text: In the ancient tongue they were called Sparks; in the modern terminology of the Academy they were classified as Nodes. But the underlying cosmic truth was identical: each civilization had adapted to the harshest, most extreme frontiers of the world—the crushing ocean depths, the volcanic island calderas, the lightning-swept mountain peaks, the sandstone canyon aqueducts, the floating sky-ziggurats, and the living root-forests.

speaker: Narrator
text: In isolation, each spark was finite, vulnerable to stagnation, and destined to suffocate under its own comfort. But when woven into a unified circuit, the energy was not merely additive—it was exponential, multiplying the vitality of the world beyond the reach of decay.

speaker: Narrator
text: Lomi adjusted his flat cap, studying the glowing runic coordinates shining across Mwaza-Kasa's shell.

speaker: Narrator
text: "Harmony kept expecting massive power surges with every node they logged," Lomi murmured, his mechanical intuition piercing the heart of the mystery.

speaker: Narrator
text: "But until all six clans are found and reconnected, the circuit is choked. We've only been drawing a fractional trickle through the dust. That's why the arena spires failed. That's why the storm tore through the shields.".

speaker: Narrator
text: "And when they are connected?"

speaker: Narrator
text: Ignatius asked, embers glowing warmly in his eyes as he looked toward the dark canopy above.

speaker: Narrator
text: "What happens when every clan on the map is found?".

speaker: Narrator
text: "Then we keep going," Lomi said simply, a broad, easy smile spreading across his soot-smudged face.

speaker: Narrator
text: "We build faster rigs. We chart uncharted oceans. And if there is no land left on this continent, we build vessels that can sail through the stars to find other worlds.".

speaker: Aggie
text: "Exploration isn't a trade or an academy degree," Aggie whispered, resting her palm gently against the rough, warm keratin of the tortoise's front leg.

speaker: Narrator
text: "It's the only thing keeping the heart of this world beating.".

speaker: Narrator
text: Rill stepped to the center of the mossy stone stairs, looking across the sacred clearing at the assembled eleven companions.

speaker: Narrator
text: "If we connect them all," Rill said softly, her blue hair stirring in the rising evening wind, "then we stabilize the resonance decay. The sickness halts. The barriers fall.

speaker: Narrator
text: And the clans can finally come home."

speaker: Narrator
text: She paused, meeting their eyes one by one in the twilight glow.

speaker: Narrator
text: "I get it now, Momentum is life.".
